rag.description: Add a wait inside an InvokeInputActions gesture, between two of its actions. The step checks the duration before anything is sent, accepts milliseconds or a time span from flow parameters, and keeps keys and buttons held while waiting, so long presses and hover menus run reliably.

qa.answer: It adds one pause to the input sequence of its InvokeInputActions container, so the driver waits between two actions.
qa.question: What does the AddPause plugin do?

qa.answer: Duration sets the wait as milliseconds or as a time span and defaults to 0; the plain argument works as well. It stores no outputs.
qa.question: What are the key parameters and outputs of AddPause?

qa.answer: It runs as an InputAction task step with the stopwatch icon and the ActionRuleModel, only as a child rule of InvokeInputActions, between the two actions it separates.
qa.question: How does AddPause fit into an automation workflow?

qa.answer: Use it for waits inside a gesture only, keep the total time under the driver timeout, and use an ordinary wait step between gestures.
qa.question: What are best practices for using AddPause?

qa.answer: Use $type “Action” with pluginName “AddPause” and set the wait in the argument, as 500 or as {{$ --Duration:00:00:02}}, inside the rules of InvokeInputActions.
qa.question: How is an AddPause rule configured?

qa.answer: Text that is not a duration, or a negative value, fails the step, and the container then sends nothing. Outside InvokeInputActions the step fails with a message that names the container.

description: ### Purpose
AddPause makes the driver wait in the middle of a gesture.
It runs only inside InvokeInputActions, and the wait happens on the driver side, between two actions of the same sequence.
Flows use it to hold a press, to let a hover menu open, and to give a page time to react during a drag.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature | Description |
| Timed wait | Waits a whole number of milliseconds, such as `500`, or a time span, such as `00:00:02`. |
| State kept | Leaves pressed keys and buttons down during the wait. |
| Inside the sequence | Waits between two actions of one request, which a separate wait step cannot do. |
| Checked before sending | Fails on text that is not a duration, and the container then sends nothing. |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case | Description |
| Long press | Hold a button for a second to open a menu that needs a held press. |
| Hover menus | Wait for a menu to open before the pointer moves to an item that is already in the page. |
| Paced drags | Wait over a drop target until it highlights. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case | Description |
| Timing checks | Verify that a long press and a short press give different results. |
| Animation checks | Wait for an animation that starts on hover before the next action. |
| Debounce checks | Verify that a page ignores input that arrives faster than its debounce time. |
### Platform
This plugin currently supports **Web** only.
Desktop and mobile drivers are not supported yet.

annotations.expected_result: The driver waits 500 milliseconds before the next action of the sequence.
annotations.notes: The step runs only inside InvokeInputActions. Between a press and a release it turns a click into a long press.

description: ### Wait half a second
The plain argument sets the wait in milliseconds.
Keys and buttons that are down stay down during the wait.

annotations.expected_result: The driver waits two seconds before the next action of the sequence.
annotations.notes: A time span is written as hours, minutes, and seconds. The whole sequence must still finish within the command timeout of the driver.

description: ### Wait two seconds through the Duration parameter
The Duration parameter sets the wait as a time span.
Use this form when the value comes from a flow parameter or a macro.

annotations.expected_result: The sequence gains one empty step, and the next action runs right after the previous one.
annotations.notes: A zero pause is rarely needed. Set a duration whenever the page needs time between two actions.

description: ### Add an empty step without waiting
A rule without an argument adds a pause of zero milliseconds.
It adds one empty step to the sequence and changes no key or button.
Sets how long the driver waits before the next action.
Accepts a whole number of milliseconds, such as `500`, or a time span, such as `00:00:02`.
Defaults to 0, and a negative value or text that is not a duration fails the step.
parameters.name: Duration

description: Holds the wait, as plain text such as `500` or as `{{$ --Duration:500}}`.
A rule without an argument adds a pause of zero milliseconds.
properties.name: Argument

summary: Adds a pause to the sequence of its InvokeInputActions container.
Waits a whole number of milliseconds or a time span between the action before it and the action after it.
Keeps every key and button as it is during the wait, which is how long presses and paced gestures are built.
